title: The Well of Cold Spring
premise: Folklorist Isandro Okonkwo has spent three years in Cold Spring documenting songs the villagers refuse to sing twice, rationalizing every wrongness as habit or superstition. When a church bell that was melted down in 1911 begins ringing at night, he learns the village survives by an annual tithe to something beneath the well—and in 1974, his own mother took what should have been returned: her sister's place. As the harvest moon rises, Isandro must descend and offer himself in her stead, but the thing below, having waited fifty years for love rather than duty, accepts instead the truth of who was taken, freeing the village at the cost of Isandro's memory of ever belonging there.
about_author: Juniper Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in Appalachian hollows before turning to fiction. They write horror about the debts communities quietly pay, and live somewhere with very old trees.

chapters.title: The Bell That Was Not Cast
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Recording elderly Marta Voss singing a lullaby she refuses to repeat, Isandro hears the melted-down church bell toll at midnight. The villagers deny hearing it; Marta's face goes gray with recognition. Emotional beat: unease curdling into dread as Isandro realizes his three years of rationalizations were shelter, not safety.

chapters.title: What Was Taken in 1974
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, interwoven with Marta's fragmented memories. Digging through parish records, Isandro finds his mother's name beside a vanished aunt, Edith, last seen at the well during harvest 1974. Villagers begin leaving offerings on his doorstep—apologies, not gifts. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of discovering your family is the village's original sin.

chapters.title: The Harvest Tithe
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. On the eve of the harvest moon, the whole village gathers at the well in silence, expecting Isandro to descend and restore the balance his mother broke. He learns the thing below doesn't want blood—it wants what was promised: someone who chooses to stay. Emotional beat: terror giving way to a terrible clarity about duty, inheritance, and love.

chapters.title: Cold Spring Rising
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV dissolving into the well-thing's ancient voice. Descending, Isandro offers himself, but speaks Edith's name aloud—the truth the village buried. The entity, starved for acknowledgment rather than flesh, takes the confession and releases its claim. Isandro surfaces at dawn, alive but unable to remember why he came. Emotional beat: bittersweet survival—saved by love, unmade by forgetting.
